subject: Tenant failover attribution and SLA credit proposal

Date: 2027-10-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Incident 2027-10-03 - failover, KV cache loss and SLA request

Olga,

Thanks for taking this. On 2027-10-03 at ~02:45 UTC we observed a coordinated failover on our tenant that coincided with a CloudPeer peering flapping event. The result for our service was a ~7 minute window of elevated error rates and token-generation latency that impacted two critical endpoints (chat & embeddings).

Our operations team collected logs and we attached an archive (orbithealth-outage-logs.tar.gz). From our tally this meets Redwood's definition of a partial degradation that should be eligible for an uptime credit under section 3.2 of our SLA. We need an apportionment explanation if you believe third-party peering is the primary cause—please include the math you used to arrive at any credit.

Requested: clear statement of attribution, proposed credit percentage, and timeline for applying credit to our invoice.

—Tim
Tim Clarke

Date: 2027-10-06T10:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Incident 2027-10-03 - failover, KV cache loss and SLA request

Team / Tim — I dug into the traces and infra signals. Summary of findings (high level):

- Timeline: 02:44:32 UTC — CloudPeer BGP session flapped across multiple egresses.
  02:44:45 UTC — Redwood's control plane initiated tenant failover for OrbitHealth due to elevated error ratios observed at edge layer.
  02:45:10 to 02:52:05 UTC — KV-cache misses and prefix rehydration caused token-latency spikes; several generation requests retried or timed out.

- Measured impact: 7m55s where average token latency increased ~3.7x and error rate increased to 6.1% (baseline 0.2%). The runtime logs show cache eviction and cold-start behavior tied to the failover sequence.

- Attribution: this was a two-factor event: the initial network instability (CloudPeer) triggered Redwood's failover logic. The control plane action (tenant relocation) amplified impact because the KV cache and in-memory context were invalidated during failover.

Proposed apportionment approach (technical rationale):
- We model the user-facing degradation as composed of: network-induced reachability loss (external) + service failover amplification (Redwood).
- Conservative split proposal for credit calculation: 60% CloudPeer / 40% Redwood. Rationale: CloudPeer's BGP instability is the root trigger; however the magnitude of the customer impact is materially increased by our failover path rehydration costs.

Data used: token-level latency histogram, request counts pre/post window, and control-plane action logs. I can share the calculation sheet (internal) — Marissa will surface a customer-ready version.

Notes/next steps:
- If OrbitHealth has their own network telemetry that demonstrates longer reachability loss, we can re-evaluate split.
- If legal/finance needs a deterministic formula we can switch to time-weighted token loss instead of a percentage split.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Runtime & Serving
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Tim Clarke <tim.clarke@orbithealth.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-08T15:32:00Z
Subject: Proposed credit calculation for 2027-10-03 partial degradation

Hi Tim — thanks for your patience while we reviewed. Attached is a customer-ready summary and a proposed credit calculation (proposed-credit-calculation.xlsx). Highlights: 

- Event window agreed: 02:44:45 — 02:52:05 UTC (7m20s).
- Token-impact method used: measured token-seconds above baseline during event window.
- Using Rishi's conservative split (40% Redwood responsibility) yields a proposed credit of 25% of the monthly invoice for the affected services.

We are prepared to apply the credit to your November invoice and to expedite the bookkeeping if you prefer a prorated one-off refund. Additional goodwill: we can provide a complimentary month of Dedicated capacity for the two affected endpoints for one month (if OrbitHealth wants to test isolation benefits).

Attachments: proposed-credit-calculation.xlsx (spreadsheet), cloudpeer-peering-report.pdf (supporting BGP timeline). Please review and let us know whether the 25% credit is acceptable or if you want us to escalate to a legal/finance review for a different split.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Tim Clarke <tim.clarke@orbithealth.com>

Subject: Re: Proposed credit calculation for 2027-10-03 partial degradation

Marissa / Olga — thanks for the breakdown and the goodwill offer. I reviewed the sheet and the CloudPeer report. OrbitHealth accepts Redwood's acknowledgment of partial responsibility, but we believe a 30% credit is a closer fit to the customer impact given downstream retries and lost business calls during the 7m window.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can move to 30% or if you want to keep the 25% and proceed with the Dedicated-capacity trial? We are happy to accept the trial if it comes with an SLA annexe guaranteeing reduced failover amplification.

If you can reply with final decision by EOD Friday 2027-10-15, we'll close the incident on our side.

—Tim
Head of Platform Engineering, OrbitHealth
